1) Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
2) Boil cabbage leaves 2 minutes; drain.
3) In large bowl, combine 1 cup cooked rice, egg, milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper.
4) Place about 1/4 cup of meat mixture in center of each cabbage leaf, and roll up, tucking in ends.
5) Place rolls in slow cooker.
6) In a small bowl, mix together tomato sauce, brown sugar, lemon juice, and Worcestershire sauce.
7) Pour over cabbage rolls.
8) Cover, and cook on low 8 to 9 hours.

1) In a large pot, combine apple juice, apple cider, sugar and cinnamon sticks.
2) Bring to a boil, then remove from heat and let cool completely.
3) When juice mixture is cool, stir in the grain alcohol.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Place carrots and onions in a pot with enough lightly salted water to cover, and bring to a boil.
3) Cook 5 minutes, or until tender but firm.
4) Drain, and spread 1/2 the carrots and onions in a baking dish.
5) Cover with 3/4 cup cheese, layer with remaining carrots and onions, and top with remaining cheese.
6) In a saucepan, melt 3 tablespoons butter and mix in flour until smooth.
7) Gradually stir in milk until thickened, and season with salt and pepper.
8) Pour over the carrots, onions, and cheese in the baking dish.
9) Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a small pot, and mix in bread crumbs.
10) Sprinkle evenly in the baking dish.
11) Bake 20 minutes in the preheated oven, or until bubbly and lightly browned.

**R**ecipe **I**nstruction **Se**mantics **C**orpus 

This dataset contains 260 cooking recipe texts which are the same as [CURD](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~ark/CURD/) and [SIMMR](https://camel.abudhabi.nyu.edu/simmr/). The corpus development is detailed in [our short paper](https://www.aclweb.org/anthology/2020.aacl-main.82). If our work contributes to your research, please cite the paper.

1) Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water.
2) Bring water to a boil and immediately remove from heat.
3) Cover and let eggs stand in hot water for 10 to 12 minutes.
4) Remove from hot water, cool, peel and chop finely.
5) In a mixing bowl, combine tuna, crabmeat, mayonnaise, sour cream and mustard.
6) Stir in chopped egg, dill weed, lemon pepper, dill and sweet relish and chopped onion.
7) Mix thoroughly.

1) In a large saucepan over medium heat, heat peanut oil.
2) Stir in garlic, ginger, lemon grass, red pepper, coriander and cumin and cook until fragrant, 2 minutes.
3) Stir in chicken and onion and cook, stirring, until chicken is white and onion is translucent, 5 minutes.
4) Stir in bok choy and cook until it begins to wilt, 5 to 10 minutes.
5) Stir in water, coconut milk, fish sauce and cilantro.
6) Simmer until chicken is thoroughly cooked and flavors are well blended, 30 minutes.

1) In a medium bowl combine apples, blueberries, sugar substitute, and the 1/4 teaspoon apple pie spice; set aside.
2) In another medium bowl stir together whole wheat pastry flour, kosher salt, and the 1/8 teaspoon apple pie spice.
3) Add oil and milk all at once to flour mixture.
4) Stir lightly with a fork until dough comes together.
5) Divide dough into 6 portions.
6) Using six 3 1/2- to 4-inch individual tart pans with removable bottoms, press one dough portion on the bottom and up the side of each tart pan.
7) Divide fruit mixture among pastry-lined pans.
8) Place tart pans on a large baking sheet.
9) Place a large piece of foil over tart pans; press down lightly around the edges to seal.
10) Bake in a 375 degrees F oven for 20 minutes; remove foil.
11) Bake about 20 minutes more or until fruit is tender.
12) Let cool in tart pans on a wire rack for 15 minutes.
13) Carefully remove sides of tart pans.
14) Serve warm or cool.

1) Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
2) Grease a cookie sheet.
3) In a medium saucepan, combine 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water.
4) Bring to a boil, stirring until butter melts completely.
5) Reduce heat to low, and add flour and salt.
6) Stir vigorously until mixture leaves the sides of the pan and begins to form a stiff ball.
7) Remove from heat.
8) Add eggs, one at a time, beating well to incorporate completely after each addition.
9) With a spoon or a pastry bag fitted with a No. 10, or larger, tip, spoon or pipe dough onto cookie sheet in 1 1/2 x 4 inch strips.
10) Bake 15 minutes in the preheated oven, then reduce heat to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) and bake 20 minutes more, until hollow sounding when lightly tapped on the bottom.
11) Cool completely on a wire rack.
12) For the filling, combine pudding mix and milk in medium bowl according to package directions.
13) In a separate bowl, beat the cream with an electric mixer until soft peaks form.
14) Beat in 1/4 cup confectioners' sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
15) Fold whipped cream into pudding.
16) Cut tops off of cooled pastry shells with a sharp knife.
17) Fill shells with pudding mixture and replace tops.
18) For the icing, melt the chocolate and 2 tablespoons butter in a medium saucepan over low heat.
19) Stir in 1 cup confectioners' sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
20) Stir in hot water, one tablespoon at a time, until icing is smooth and has reached desired consistency.
21) Remove from heat, cool slightly, and drizzle over filled eclairs.
22) Refrigerate until serving.

1) Combine condensed milk, milk, cream, vanilla, salt and fruit in freezer canister of ice cream maker.
2) Freeze according to manufacturer's directions.

1) In a large mixing bowl, combine 3 cups flour, cheese, sugar, yeast and salt.
2) Add milk and egg; beat on low speed until smooth.
3) Stir in enough remaining flour to form a soft dough.
4) Turn onto a floured surface; knead until smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes.
5) Place in a greased bowl, turning once to grease top.
6) Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
7) Punch dough down.
8) Divide in half and shape into two loaves.
9) Place in two greased 9-in.
10) Cover and let rise until doubled, about 45 minutes.
11) Bake at 375 degrees F for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.
12) Remove from pans to cool on wire racks.

1) Place whole potatoes in their skins into a large pot of boiling water; boil for 25 to 30 minutes.
2) Remove potatoes, and discard water.
3) When cool enough to handle, peel potatoes, and place on a lightly floured surface.
4) Mash potatoes with a rolling pin.
5) Place mashed potatoes into a large bowl.
6) Stir in flour, egg, parsley, salt, and nutmeg.
7) Knead well to form a smooth dough.
8) Then roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/2 inch.
9) Cut flattened dough into thin strips, about 1 1/2 inches long.
10) Gently roll out the strips, or stretch them until the ends taper.
11) Set aside for 15 minutes.
12) In a large skillet, heat lard over medium heat.
13) Place the potato strips into the skillet, and fry until golden brown on both sides.

1) Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil.
2) Cook pasta for 8 to 10 minutes, or until al dente; drain.
3) In a large skillet, brown beef over medium heat.
4) Drain fat from pan, and transfer meat to a bowl.
5) In the same skillet, cook onion and bell pepper in butter until tender.

7) Simmer for 10 minutes.
8) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

11) Repeat layers.
12) Mix together soup and beef broth until smooth, and pour over casserole.
13) Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
14) Bake in preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes, or until heated through.

1) Preheat oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C).

5) Add water to the top of beef.
6) Cover and cook in oven at 275 degrees F (135 degrees C) for 4 to 5 hours.
7) When meat is cooked, shred meat with 2 forks, add barbecue sauce and mix well.

1) Combine brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla in large bowl.
2) Beat eggs into creamed mixture.
3) In another bowl, combine flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda.
4) Mix this mixture into creamed mixture until just blended.
5) Stir in chocolate chips.
6) Drop rounded tablespoonfuls of dough onto ungreased baking sheet about 2 inches apart.
7) Place cookie sheet in the middle of the oven.
8) Cool for 2 minutes on baking sheet.
9) Remove cookies to wire rack to cool completely.

12) Cool completely, and frost cooled cookies.

1) In a large mixing bowl, combine flour and salt.

4) Add to flour mixture; combine on low speed, then beat on medium-high until smooth.
5) In another small mixing bowl and with clean beaters, beat egg whites on high until stiff peaks form.
6) Gently fold into batter.
7) Bake in a preheated waffle iron according to manufacturer's directions.
8) Serve with warm maple syrup or fresh fruit in season.

1) Preheat the oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C).
2) Place ham in a roasting pan.
3) Pour in water to a 2 inch depth.
4) Cover with a tight fitting lid.
5) Bake for 6 to 8 hours in the preheated oven (all day or all night).
6) Remove from the oven, pour off drippings and reserve.
7) Debone ham, removing any excess fat as well, and return to the roasting pan.
8) Skim fat from the top of the drippings, and discard.
9) In a small bowl, mix one cup of the drippings with honey, brown sugar, liquid smoke, Worcestershire sauce and cloves.
10) Pour this over the ham, cover and return to the oven.
11) Remaining drippings may be discarded or reserved for other uses.
12) Bake for another 30 to 40 minutes in the preheated oven.
13) Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

1) In a large skillet over medium heat, combine chicken, lemonade, olive oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce.
2) Season with garlic powder, onion powder, and bay leaf.
3) Simmer until chicken is no longer pink, and juices run clear, 15 to 20 minutes.
4) Meanwhile, warm the tortillas in the oven or microwave until soft.
5) When chicken is fully cooked, transfer to serving bowl.
6) Place lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, salsa, and sour cream in serving dishes.
7) Each person can create their own wrap, using their preferred ingredients.

1) Bring water to boil in a large pot.
2) Place beef shank in, and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
3) Let cool overnight.
4) Lift meat out, trim off gristle and cut meat into medium sized pieces; set aside.
5) Skim fat from surface of stock, or strain through a fine sieve.
6) Return stock to heat, and bring to a boil.
7) Add onions, carrots and rutabaga.
8) Season with salt and pepper.
9) Simmer for 1 hour.
10) Add potatoes, and simmer until tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
11) Stir in the leeks, cabbage, parsley and reserved meat.
12) Simmer 10 minutes, or until cabbage is tender.

1) Place the warm water in a small bowl, and sprinkle the yeast over the top.
2) Let stand until yeast has dissolved and is foamy, about 15 minutes.
3) Measure flour into a large bowl.
4) Make a well in the center, and pour in the yeast mixture and cold water.
5) Use a sturdy spoon to mix it together until sticky and difficult to stir, but nevertheless thoroughly combined.
6) Cover and allow to ferment for 24 hours in the refrigerator before using.
7) Store in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Grease and flour 2 (9 inch) pans.
3) Sift together the flour, baking soda and salt.
4) Set aside.
5) In the top of a double boiler, heat 6 ounces chocolate, stirring occasionally, until chocolate is melted and smooth.
6) Remove from heat and allow to cool to lukewarm.
7) In a large bowl, cream together the butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy.
8) Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in 1 1/2 teaspoon vanilla.
9) Stir in the melted chocolate.
10) Beat in the flour mixture alternately with the sour cream.
11) Stir in boiling water (batter will be thin).
12) Pour batter into prepared pans.
13) Bake in the preheated oven for 35 to 40 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean.
14) Let cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely.
15) Make the Chocolate Buttercream Frosting: In the top of a double boiler, heat 6 ounces chocolate, stirring occasionally, until chocolate is melted and smooth.
16) In a large bowl, whip the butter for about 10 minutes until it is super fluffy, beat in egg yolk.
17) Gradually blend in the confectioners' sugar, alternating with 2 tablespoons vanilla and 2 tablespoons cream, then blend in the melted chocolate.
18) Beat in the softened cream cheese.
19) Make the Ganache: In a large saucepan, combine chocolate chips and 1 cup heavy cream.
20) Heat, stirring constantly, until chocolate is melted and smooth.
21) Remove from heat and set aside.
22) Assemble the cake: When cake is completely cooled, cover the bottom cake layer with as much ganache as desired.
23) Refrigerate for 5 minutes, or until ganache has set.
24) Spread frosting over the ganache.
25) Cover with top layer of cake.
26) Frost top and sides with buttercream, and garnish with more ganache.

1) DAY BEFORE: Cream butter and cream cheese together until smoothly blended.
2) Beat in the flour.
3) Shape dough into a smooth ball, wrap in foil or cling wrap, and refrigerate overnight or up to a week.
4) AT BAKING TIME: Remove dough from refrigerator 30 minutes before using.
5) Start heating oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
6) Roll chilled dough thin.
7) Cut with 3 or 4 inch round cookie cutter.
8) Place small spoonful of jam in center of each round, moisten edges with water.
9) Fold round over and press edges together.
10) Bake on ungreased cookie sheet 15 to 20 minutes.
11) Immediately roll in sugar mixed with cinnamon (traditional) OR in confectioners' sugar if preferred.

1) Cook pork in a large wok over medium-high heat.
2) Drain and set aside.
3) In a large bowl, mix the cabbage, carrot, green bell pepper, onion, garlic and ginger.
4) In a small bowl, mix the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses until smooth.
5) Heat 2 tablespoons oil in wok.
6) Stir in cabbage mixture in batches, cooking each batch 3 to 4 minutes, just until tender.
7) Return vegetables to bowl, and mix in pork.
8) Stir in the cornstarch mixture.
9) Heat 1 quart oil in a deep fryer to 365 degrees F (185 degrees C).
10) Place about 1 tablespoon filling on each egg roll wrapper.
11) Fold one corner of wrapper over filling.
12) Fold wrapper sides over filling.
13) Roll wrappers to form egg rolls.
14) Fry egg rolls in batches in the hot oil until golden brown.
15) Drain on paper towels and serve with sweet and sour sauce.

8) Place on prepared sheets and let rest at room temperature several hours, until set.

1) In a large skillet, heat oil.
2) Add 1/2 of the garlic.
3) Season flour with poultry seasoning.
4) Dredge chicken parts in flour, then brown in the skillet for 4 or 5 minutes.
5) Add the sausage, and saute for a few minutes.
6) Add the onion, carrots, mushrooms, rosemary and the remaining garlic.
7) Stir all together.
8) Add the wine and tomatoes; stir.
9) Cover and let simmer over low heat for 25 minutes.
10) Season with salt and pepper to taste and let simmer for another 10 minutes.
11) Let cool covered for 10 minutes, then serve.

1) In a bowl, sift together the flour, light brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt.
2) Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
3) Sprinkle with the ice water, and toss the mixture with a fork until evenly moistened.
4) Pat into a round, and wrap in plastic.
5) Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
6) In the top half of a double boiler, heat the milk until it begins to bubble.
7) In a bowl, beat together the egg whites, sugar, and 1 tablespoon of the hot milk.
8) Whisk the egg white mixture into the remaining hot milk.
9) Cook and stir without boiling about 10 minutes, until the mixture is thick enough to coat the back of a metal spoon.
10) Remove from heat, and stir in the vanilla.
11) Cool to room temperature.
12) Preheat oven to 375  degrees F (190 degrees C).
13) Lightly grease an 8 inch tart pan with a removable bottom.
14) On a floured surface, roll the tart dough out to 1/4 inch thickness.
15) Press the chilled dough into the prepared tart pan.
16) Trim the edges, and pierce the bottom with a fork.
17) Bake 15 to 18 minutes in the preheated oven, until golden brown.
18) Remove to a wire rack, and cool completely.
19) Spoon the filling mixture into the crust.
20) Bake 18 to 20 minutes in the preheated oven.
21) Cool to room temperature on a wire rack.
22) Refrigerate 8 hours.

1) In a small bowl, stir the food coloring into the evaporated milk.
2) Paint onto cookies with a paintbrush before baking.

1) Cut a pocket in each slice of bread.
2) Open carefully
3) In a large bowl, combine the ricotta, cottage cheese and cream cheese.
4) Add the sugar and flavoring extract and beat until smooth.
5) Spread the mixture evenly into each bread pocket.
6) Beat together the egg substitutes and milk.
7) Dip the slices of bread in the egg mixture.
8) Heat a nonstick pan over medium-high heat.
9) Coat with cooking spray.
10) Cook the toast on each side for about 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown.

1) Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
2) Grease and flour a 9x5 inch loaf pan.
3) In a large bowl, combine dates, brown sugar, margarine and boiling water.
4) Let stand 15 minutes.
5) Stir in flour, soda and vanilla.
6) Pour batter into prepared pan.
7) Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes.
8) Allow to cool.

1) Preheat an oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
2) Grease cookie sheets.
3) In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt butter till lightly browned.
4) Pour into medium sized bowl.
5) Stir in the egg white, sugar and vanilla.
6) Combine the flour cocoa, and salt; mix into the butter mixture.
7) Fold in chocolate.
8) Drop by teaspoonfuls about 2 inches apart onto cookie sheets.
9) Bake for 12 to 15 minutes.
10) Transfer to rack to cool and dust with confectioners' sugar.

1) Prepare biscuits (enough to make 4 cups crumbled), and one 8x8 inch pan cornbread according to package directions.
2) Cool and crumble.
3) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
4) In a small pot, combine onion, celery, margarine and chicken broth.
5) Bring to boil and cook vegetables until tender.

7) Pour broth and vegetables over bread mixture, and stir until combined.
8) Bake in the preheated oven for 30 to 45 minutes.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Place bacon in a skillet and cook over medium heat until the pieces are browned.
3) Remove with a slotted spoon to paper towels.
4) Discard all but 1 tablespoon of bacon grease.
5) Stir in onions and mushrooms, and cook until soft.
6) Remove from heat.
7) In a large bowl, stir together beef, egg, and milk.
8) Stir in the onion and mushrooms.
9) Mix in about 4 ounces of Swiss cheese, and all but 1 tablespoon of bacon.
10) Stir in cornflake crumbs, and mix until well blended.
11) Shape into a loaf, and place in a meatloaf pan.
12) Bake in a preheated oven for 1 hour.
13) Drain fat, and sprinkle with remaining cheese and bacon.
14) Return to oven, and bake until cheese is melted, about 5 minutes.

1) Preheat your oven's broiler.
2) In a medium bowl, stir together the onion, tomato, celery, bell pepper, cheese, chili powder and salt.
3) Arrange slices of bread on a baking sheet or broiling pan.
4) Top each one with 1/4 of the mixture, spreading out to the edges.
5) Broil for 4 to 5 minutes, or until cheese melts.
6) Watch closely to prevent burning.
7) Serve immediately.

1) In a large skillet over medium heat, brown chicken and potatoes in oil for 10-15 minutes.
2) Remove chicken and potatoes; set aside.
3) Discard all but 1 tablespoon drippings.
4) To drippings, add cream, salt and pepper; stir to mix.
5) Return chicken and potatoes to skillet.
6) Sprinkle with onions and dill.
7) Cover and simmer for 50-60 minutes or until chicken juices run clear and potatoes are tender.
8) With a slotted spoon, remove chicken and potatoes to a serving platter; keep warm.
9) Add sour cream to pan; stir to mix and heat through.
10) Serve with chicken and potatoes.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Beat the butter or margarine with the white and brown sugars until light and fluffy.

10) Cool in pan on a wire rack then cut into squares.

1) In a greased 11-in. baking dish, combine the broth, rice, Italian seasoning and garlic powder.
2) Cover and bake at 375 degrees F for 10 minutes.
3) Add the broccoli, Parmesan cheese and half of the onions.
4) Top with fish fillets; sprinkle with paprika.
5) Cover and bake 20-25 minutes longer or until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
6) Uncover; sprinkle with cheddar cheese and remaining onions.
7) Return to the oven for 3 minutes or until cheese is melted.

1) Peel and dice apples.
2) Add sugar and cinnamon.
3) Cook in a saucepan on low heat.
4) Cook until soft, then mash with fork to form a thick applesauce.
5) Sift flour and salt together.
6) Cut in the shortening.
7) Add water and mix with fork.
8) Roll out to about 1/8 inch thick on a floured board.
9) Cut with a large cookie cutter (4 inches in diameter).
10) In each round, place 1 heaping tablespoon fruit.
11) Moisten edges with cold water, fold and press edge with a fork.
12) Heat oil in a large skillet on medium-high heat.
13) Fry pies, a few at a time, 2 to 3 minutes on each side; cook until golden brown.
14) Drain on paper towels.
15) Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.

1) In a large mixing bowl, dissolve yeast in 1/2 cup of water.
2) Add sugar, oil, salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and remaining water; beat until smooth.
3) Add enough remaining all-purpose flour to form a soft dough.
4) Turn onto a floured surface; knead until smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes.
5) Place in a greased bowl, turning once to grease top.
6) Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
7) Punch dough down.
8) Divide in half.
9) On a greased baking sheet, flatten each half to 1-in.
10) Pierce each loaf several times with a fork.
11) Cover and let rise in a warm place until nearly doubled, about 30 minutes.
12) Bake at 375 degrees F for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

1) Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
2) Season both sides of chicken with Cajun seasoning, and place in hot oil.
3) Stir in crushed garlic.
4) Cook chicken 5 minutes on each side, or until juices run clear.
5) Remove chicken from skillet, drain on paper towels, cool slightly, and dice; discard oil and garlic.
6) In a small bowl, mix remaining olive oil, balsamic vinegar, mustard, salt, and pepper.
7) In a large bowl, gently toss the dressing with the mixed salad greens, arugula, avocado, sun-dried tomatoes, and olives.
8) Top with diced chicken to serve.

1) Butter a 9x13 inch baking dish.
2) Arrange the slices of bread in the bottom.
3) In a large bowl, beat together eggs, milk, cream, vanilla and cinnamon.
4) Pour over bread slices, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
5) The next morning, preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
6) In a small saucepan, combine butter, brown sugar and corn syrup; heat until bubbling.
7) Pour over bread and egg mixture.
8) Bake in preheated oven, uncovered, for 40 minutes.

3) Stand remaining cookies around edge of pan.
4) Spread 3/4 cup fudge topping over crust.
5) Freeze 15 minutes.

8) Freeze 30 minutes.
9) Scoop remaining quart of ice cream into balls and arrange over spread ice cream layer.
10) Freeze until firm, 4 hours or overnight.
11) To serve, garnish with remainder of fudge topping, whipped cream and cherries.

1) Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
2) Slice the top of the head of garlic, just enough to remove paper and expose the tops of the cloves.
3) Drizzle with olive oil and roast in preheated oven, either in a clay garlic roaster or wrapped in aluminum foil.
4) Roast for 20 minutes or until cloves are soft and slip from skins when pushed.
5) Change oven setting to broil (375 degrees F, 190 degrees C).
6) Let garlic cool.
7) To prepare chicken, place in a 9x13 inch baking dish and splash both sides with white wine.
8) Broil for 25 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and juices run clear.
9) Meanwhile, place butter or margarine and milk in a large skillet and heat over medium heat until warm.
10) Stir in the flour and cheese.
11) Stir over medium heat until sauce begins to thicken.
12) Slip cooled garlic cloves from skin and add to the sauce (if desired, mince first).
13) Add chopped parsley.
14) Bring nearly to a boil; reduce heat and stir to control thickening.
15) If desired, pour sauce over cooked rice or pasta and top with broiled chicken.
16) Enjoy!

1) Place frozen burritos in a greased 13-in baking dish; set aside.
2) In a saucepan, melt butter.
3) Stir in flour until smooth; gradually stir in water.
4) Bring to a boil; cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thickened.
5) Add the tomato sauce, chili powder, bouillon, cumin and salt.
6) Simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes or until thickened.
7) Pour over the burritos.
8) Sprinkle with cheese, olives if desired and onions.
9) Bake, uncovered, at 350 degrees F for 35-40 minutes or until heated through.

1) Melt 1/4 cup of butter in a large skillet over medium heat.

8) Season with cayenne pepper.
9) Bring to a low boil, and simmer 5 minutes to blend flavors.

1) Slice chicken breasts in thirds horizontally to make 12 thin chicken fillets.
2) Lightly pound each piece.
3) Place in a dish, and pour milk over them.
4) Soak for 10 minutes.
5) In a shallow bowl, stir together the bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese and parsley.
6) Set aside.
7) Heat olive oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
8) Dredge chicken pieces in the bread crumb mixture, and place in the hot oil.
9) Quickly brown on both sides, then remove to a buttered 9x13 inch baking dish, or similar size.
10) Season with salt and pepper to taste.
11) Place orange slices over the top of the chicken.
12) Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
13) Drain the oil from the skillet, reserving 1/4 cup.
14) Heat the reserved oil with the wine over medium heat until reduced by 1/2.
15) Add broth and orange juice, and reduce by 1/2 again.
16) Pour the sauce over the chicken, then drizzle with Grand Marinier.
17) Bake for 20 to 25 minutes in the preheated oven, until bubbly.

1) Place mushrooms and chicken in a slow cooker.
2) Add the celery, zucchini, carrots, onion, tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika and pepper.
3) Cover and cook on low for 5 hours or until meat juices run clear.
4) Remove chicken and vegetables and keep warm.
5) Transfer cooking juices to a saucepan; skim fat.
6) Combine the cornstarch and water until smooth; add to the juices.
7) Bring to a boil; cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thickened.
8) Pour over chicken and vegetables; serve over rice.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray or grease one 9x13 inch pan.
2) Prepare the topping by mixing together the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and chopped pecans.
3) Sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
4) Blend together butter and sugar; add eggs and beat well; Add apple butter, vanilla, wheat germ or bran cereal; Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with sour cream; mix well after each addition.
5) Bake for 40 minutes.
6) Pour 1/2 batter into pan, sprinkle 1/2 the topping over top; Pour remaining batter and top with remaining topping.

1) In a microwave, melt butterscotch chips; cool for 10 minutes.
2) In a mixing bowl, cream butter and sugars.
3) Add egg, milk and vanilla; mix well.
4) Beat in melted chips.
5) Gradually add flour; mix well.
6) Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
7) On a floured surface, roll out dough to 1/4-in. thickness.
8) Cut with a floured 4-1/2-in. gingerbread man cookie cutter and a 3-in. round cutter.
9) Place 2 in. apart on greased baking sheets.
10) Bake at 375 degrees F for 5-8 minutes or until edges are lightly browned.
11) Cool for 1 minute; remove to wire racks to cool completely.
12) For frosting, combine shortening, water, flour and vanilla in a mixing bowl; mix well.
13) gradually beat in sugar.
14) Place 1 cup frosting in a plastic bag; cut a small hole in corner of bag.
15) Pipe shirt and shorts on players.
16) Fill in outline and smooth with a metal spatula.
17) Tint 1/4 cup frosting black; place in a plastic bag.
18) Pipe lines on round cookies to create basketballs; pipe hair, eyes and noses on players.
19) Tint 1/4 cup frosting red; pipe a mouth on each player.
20) Tint remaining frosting to match team colors of your choice; pipe around shirts and shorts and add a letter on shirts if desired.

1) In a medium bowl, combine first six ingredients.
2) Microwave on high until heated through, about 5 minutes.
3) Sprinkle on coconut, if desired.
4) Serve.

1) Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
2) Sprinkle chicken with garlic powder, and brown on both sides.
3) Remove chicken to paper towels.
4) Spoon off chicken fat, and return pan to stove.
5) Stir in mushrooms and onions; cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft.
6) Remove to a medium bowl.
7) In a separate bowl, mix together basil, oregano, rosemary, and thyme.
8) Season with garlic salt, pepper, and poultry seasoning.
9) Stir in wine, and add to onion and mushrooms.
10) Return chicken to Dutch oven.
11) Pour mushroom mixture and broth over chicken; cover, and cook over low heat until meat begins to fall off the bone, about 1 1/2 hours.

1) Combine the chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, ginger, bay leaves and peppercorns in a Dutch oven.
2) Bring to a boil over medium heat.
3) Once it boils, reduce heat to a simmer.
4) Cover the pot and simmer for 30 minutes, basting the chicken occasionally.
5) After 30 minutes, remove lid and cook until liquid has reduced to half.
6) Remove chicken from the pot to a serving plate.
7) Strain the liquid from the pot to remove all the food particles, and set aside.
8) Serve chicken hot over steamed rice and drizzle with reserved sauce.

1) In a large mixing bowl, cream the shortening and sugar.
2) Beat in the egg and molasses.
3) Combine flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon and salt; gradually add to creamed mixture.
4) Roll teaspoonfuls of dough into balls.
5) Dip one side of each ball into sugar; place with sugar side up on a greased baking sheet.
6) Bake at 350 degrees F for 12-15 minutes or until lightly browned and crinkly.

1) Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2) Roll out pastry shell and allow to rest in refrigerator.
3) Line a 9 inch pie pan with one rolled out pastry crust.
4) In a medium mixing bowl combine pie filling, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon rind.
5) Stir until fully combined and spread into pastry lined pan.
6) In a small mixer bowl combine egg, sugar, lemon juice, cream cheese, and sour cream.
7) Beat at medium speed until smooth.
8) Spread cheese mixture over apple mixture, and place top crust over filling.

10) Bake in preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden brown.
11) Cool completely before serving.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan.
3) Mix flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon.
4) Make a well in the center and add sugar, oil, eggs and vanilla.
5) Mix with wooden spoon until smooth.
6) Stir in carrots, coconut, walnuts and pineapple.
7) Pour into 9x13 inch pan.
8) Bake at 350 degrees for about 45 minutes.
9) Don't panic, the center will sink a little.
10) Allow to cool.
11) To make the frosting: Cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth.
12) Add the confectioners sugar and beat until creamy.

1) Quarter onion.
2) Chop scrubbed celery and carrot into 1 inch chunks.
3) Place chicken pieces, onion, celery, carrot, salt, and cloves in large soup pot or Dutch oven.
4) Add 6 cups water.
5) Bring to a boil.
6) Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
7) Remove chicken and vegetables.
8) Strain stock.
9) Skim fat off the surface.
10) Separate the egg white from the egg yolk, and reserve the shell.
11) In a small bowl, combine 1/4 cup cold water, egg white, and crushed eggshell.
12) Add to strained stock, and bring to a boil.
13) Remove from heat, and let stand 5 minutes.
14) Strain again through a sieve lined with cheesecloth.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Turn a 9x5 inch loaf pan or metal bowl upside down and cover the outside with foil.
3) Place onto a cookie sheet.
4) Stir together the flour, cocoa, salt and almonds; set aside.
5) In a medium bowl, cream together the butter and sugar until smooth.
6) Beat in the egg and vanilla.
7) Gradually stir in the dry ingredients to form a fairly stiff dough.
8) On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough out to 1/4 inch in thickness.
9) Cut into circles using a glass or cookie cutter.
10) Starting at the top (bottom) of the pan or bowl, arrange cookies so they are overlapping.
11) Work toward the edges covering as much of the pan as you can.
12) Be sure to press each cookie on so you will have a good solid bowl.
13) Bake for 10 to 15 minutes in the preheated oven, until cookies are firm.
14) Cool completely.
15) Carefully turn the pan over and remove the pan from the foil, then carefully remove the foil from inside the cookie structure.
16) Fill with cookie or candy.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F ( 175 degrees C).
2) Lightly grease a 9 inch springform pan.
3) In a small bowl, mix together 1 1/2 cups chocolate wafer crumbs, 2 tablespoons sugar, and melted butter.
4) Press onto the bottom and 1 1/2 inch up the sides of the prepared 9 inch springform pan.
5) Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 10 minutes.
6) Allow to cool.
7) Reduce oven temperature to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
8) To Make Filling: In a small saucepan, heat 1/4 cup whipping cream and 1/4 cup chocolate chips, stirring constantly, until chips are melted.
9) In a large mixing bowl, beat cream cheese and 1 cup of sugar until smooth.
10) Add cocoa and beat well.
11) Add eggs and beat on low until just blended.
12) Stir in 1 teaspoon vanilla and reserved chocolate mixture until blended.
13) Pour over crust.
14) Bake at 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) for 45 to 50 minutes or until center is almost set.
15) To Make Topping: In a small saucepan, heat 1/4 cup whipping cream and 1 teaspoon vanilla until just before boiling.
16) Stir constantly and be careful not to boil over.
17) Have 1 1/2 cups chocolate chips ready in a small bowl.
18) Pour in the hot cream and stir with a spoon until smooth.
19) Spread over baked cheesecake and refrigerate overnight.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Rinse pork chops, pat dry, and season with garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste.
3) Place the beaten egg and egg substitute mixture in a small bowl.
4) Dredge the pork chops lightly in flour, dip in the egg, and coat liberally with bread crumbs.
5) Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
6) Place the pork chops in the pan and coat the tops with canola cooking spray.
7) Fry the pork chops 5 minutes per side, or until the breading appears well browned.
8) Transfer the chops to a 9x13 inch baking dish, and cover with foil.
9) Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour.
10) While baking, combine the cream of mushroom soup, milk, and white wine in a medium bowl.
11) After the pork chops have baked for an hour, cover them with the soup mixture.
12) Replace foil, and bake for another 30 minutes.

1) Cut chicken breasts into 1 inch strips.
2) Place in a medium bowl with desired marinade, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
3) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
4) Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
5) Saute chicken and onions until chicken is evenly brown.
6) Stir in diced tomatoes with green chile peppers, stewed tomatoes, chile peppers, soup and broth.
7) Bring mixture to a boil.
8) Reduce heat, cover skillet, and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, or until chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear.
9) Remove chicken from skillet, and shred when cool enough to handle.
10) Meanwhile, allow skillet mixture to simmer and reduce to about 2 1/4 cups.
11) In a medium bowl, combine shredded chicken and about 1/4 cup skillet mixture (just enough to make a paste like mixture).
12) Mix together with half the chopped green onions.
13) Pour remaining 2 cups of skillet mixture into a 9x13 inch baking dish.
14) In a second skillet, heat cream over low heat, being careful not to boil.
15) Dip tortillas in the warm cream to soften and coat.
16) Spoon about 1/3 cup chicken mixture onto each tortilla.
17) Top chicken mixture with half the shredded cheese, and roll up tortillas.
18) Place rolled tortillas in baking dish, seam side down, and drizzle with enchilada sauce.
19) Cover with remaining shredded cheese, and sprinkle remaining chopped green onion over cheese.
20) Bake uncovered in preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbling.

1) Beat together cream cheese and margarine until well blended.
2) Add flour, mixing well.
3) Shape into a ball, cover and chill for 2 hours.
4) In saucepan over medium heat, cook sugar and milk, stirring occasionally until milk boils and sugar is dissolved.
5) Add the ground nuts.
6) Remove from heat and let cool until mixture is of spreading consistency.
7) Roll out chilled dough on lightly floured surface to a rectangle about 18 X 12 inches.
8) Cut in half lengthwise.
9) Spread each piece with milk/nut filling and roll up like a jelly-roll, starting from the long side.
10) Cut each roll in half.
11) Place seam side down on ungreased cookie sheets (two on a baking sheet).
12) Leaving roll's shape intact, cut into slices 1/2 inch thick almost to the bottom of the roll.
13) Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 15 to 20 minutes or till done.
14) Remove from sheet and sprinkle with confectioners' sugar.
15) Cool on racks.
16) Cut cookies all the way through.
17) Refrigerate or freeze.
18) Resprinkle with confectioners' sugar before serving.

1) In a large bowl, combine the oranges, pineapple, whipped topping, coconut, marshmallows and milk.
2) Mix together well and chill 1 hour before serving.
3) Garnish with cherries.

1) Place flour in a shallow bowl.
2) Place breadcrumbs in a separate shallow bowl, and mix with ground black pepper and cayenne pepper.
3) Place eggs and water in a small bowl.
4) One piece at a time, coat the chicken in the flour, the eggs and the bread crumbs, and set aside.
5) Heat oil in a deep fryer to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
6) In small batches, fry chicken 6 to 8 minutes, or until golden brown.
7) In a separate small bowl, combine the mayonnaise, horseradish, sour cream, Worcestershire sauce and mustard.

1) Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
2) Grease a muffin pan or line with paper muffin liners.
3) In a large mixing bowl, cream butter and brown sugar together until fluffy.
4) Add bananas, milk, vanilla and eggs; mix well.
5) Stir in flour, bran, baking powder, soda and salt; blend just until moistened.
6) Stir in walnuts.

8) Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 20 to 25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.

1) Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C).
2) Beat the eggs in a large bowl.
3) Mix in sugar, salt, vanilla, and syrup.
4) Melt the butter or margarine, and add it to the egg mixture.
5) Stir in the nuts.
6) Pour filling into pie shell.
7) Bake in preheated oven for 10 minutes.
8) Reduce heat to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C), and continue baking for 35 to 45 minutes.

1) For batter, combine the eggs, water, flour and salt in a blender.
2) Cover and process until smooth; let stand for 15 minutes.
3) Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, saute onion in butter until tender.
4) Stir in flour until blended.
5) Gradually stir in milk.
6) Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly; cook and stir for 2 minutes or until slightly thickened.
7) Reduce heat to low.
8) Stir in 1/2 cup cheese, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, pepper and salt until cheese is melted.
9) Stir in broccoli.
10) Cover; keep warm.
11) Heat a lightly greased 8-in. nonstick skillet; pour 2 tablespoons batter into the center of skillet.
12) Lift and tilt pan to evenly coat bottom.
13) Cook until top appears dry; turn and cook 15-20 seconds longer.
14) Remove to a wire rack.
15) Repeat with remaining batter, greasing skillet as needed.
16) Spoon about 1/2 cup filling down the center of each crepe; roll up.
17) Place seam side down in an ungreased 11-in. baking dish.
18) Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
19) Bake, uncovered, at 350 degrees F for 5-7 minutes or until cheese is melted.

1) In a large bowl, stir together the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon and nutmeg.
2) Make a well in the center and pour in the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla.
3) Mix until well blended.
4) Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
5) Heat oil in a deep heavy skillet or deep-fryer to 370 degrees F (185 degrees C).
6) On a floured board, roll chilled dough out to 1/2 inch thickness.
7) Use a 3 inch round cutter to cut out doughnuts.
8) Use a smaller cutter to cut holes from center.
9) Fry doughnuts in hot oil until golden brown, turning once.
10) Remove from oil to drain on paper plates.
11) Combine the remaining 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon and 1/2 cup sugar in a large resealable bag.
12) Place a few warm donuts into the bag at a time, seal and shake to coat.

1) Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
2) Place chicken in the pot; brown on all sides.
3) Season with sea salt, chili powder, cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper,  and cayenne pepper.
4) Mix in onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper.
5) Pour in about 3 cups water, and continue cooking 10 minutes, until about 1/2 the water has evaporated.
6) Mix the kidney beans, black beans, and corn into the pot.
7) Season with green pepper sauce.
8) Reduce heat to low, and mix in remaining 2 cups water and tomato paste.
9) Simmer, stirring occasionally 30 minutes, or until thickened.
10) Top with cilantro to serve.

1) Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat.
2) In a bowl, mix the ground beef, Worcestershire sauce, basil, garlic salt, and pepper.
3) Form the mixture into 4 burger patties.
4) Lightly oil the grill grate, and cook burgers about 6 minutes, turning once, to an internal temperature of 160 degrees F (70 degrees C), or to desired doneness.
5) Serve on hamburger buns.

1) In a small bowl, mix together the mustard and onion soup mix.
2) Lay out two long sheets of aluminum foil crosswise.
3) Pat the roast dry, and place in the center of the foil.
4) Generously coat the roast with the mustard mixture.
5) Wrap the foil tightly around the roast, then apply one more piece of foil to really seal it in so that the roast can be rotated without all of the juices spilling out.
6) Prepare an outdoor grill for indirect heat.
7) For charcoal, light the coals, then move to one side of the grill.
8) Place the roast on the grill, and cover.
9) Cook for about 2 hours, turning every 30 to 45 minutes, or until the internal temperature is at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).
10) Let stand for about 10 minutes before carving.
11) Place on a deep serving plate before unwrapping so you can be sure to save the juices and mustard rub to slather on the beef slices.

1) Mix oil, garlic, salt, pepper, cumin and oregano; spread paste on both sides of the lamb and let stand for an hour until meat comes to room temperature.
2) Adjust oven rack to upper or upper-middle position (depending on lamb's thickness) and preheat broiler on high for at least 10 minutes.
3) Place lamb, cut side up, on a large wire rack set over a foil-lined roasting pan.
4) Broil, moving pan so entire surface browns evenly, about 8 minutes.
5) Turn lamb over; continue to broil until well browned on the other side, about 8 minutes longer.
6) Turn off broiler, remove lamb from oven and let rest for 10 minutes.
7) Heat oven to 325 degrees.
8) Stick a meat thermometer into the thickest portion of the lamb; return it to the oven.
9) Roast for a total of 50 minutes to 1 hour, until thermometer registers a rosy-pink 140 degrees.
10) Check lamb several times after 30 minutes.
11) If lamb gets done sooner, simply turn down oven to 170 degrees until ready to serve.
12) As soon as lamb comes out of the oven, squeeze on lemon juice and sprinkle with fresh herbs.
13) Carve, slicing across the grain when possible.
14) Arrange on a platter, drizzle with accumulated juices, and serve.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Grease one 9x5 inch loaf pan.
3) Measure flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs and vanilla into large mixing bowl.
4) Beat 3 minutes.
5) Pour into prepared loaf pan.
6) Smooth top.
7) Combine 2 tablespoons white sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon and butter, mixing until crumbly.
8) Sprinkle topping over smoothed batter.
9) Using knife, cut in a light swirling motion to give a marbled effect.
10) Bake for about 50 minutes.
11) Test with toothpick.
12) When inserted it should come out clean.
13) Remove bread from pan to rack to cool.

1) In a large bowl, combine first eight ingredients.
2) Place chicken in mixture and turn to coat.
3) Cover and marinate overnight in the refrigerator.
4) Remove chicken from marinade; coat each piece with crumbs.
5) Arrange on a shallow baking pan.
6) Bake, uncovered, at 350 degrees for 45 minutes or until juices run clear.

1) Bring 6 cups of water to a boil.
2) Remove from heat, and add the almonds.
3) Let the almonds soak in water for about 5 minutes, then drain and peel.
4) Spread the almonds on baking sheets, and bake at 200 degrees F(95 degrees C) until completely dry and toasted.
5) This takes several hours, and needs to be prepared ahead.
6) Be careful not to burn the nuts, as this will give a bitter taste to the filling.
7) Combine 1 cup sugar and 1 cup water in a saucepan, and bring to a boil.
8) Add 1 teaspoon lemon juice, reduce heat to low, and let it simmer until syrupy, about 30 to 40 minutes.
9) Stir in orange blossom water, and remove from heat.
10) Set sugar syrup aside.
11) Combine flour and salt in a large mixing bowl.
12) Make a hole in the center, and pour oil, egg, 1/2 teaspoon lemon juice, and 1 tablespoon orange blossom water into the center.
13) Mix with fingers until the dough resembles coarse crumbs.
14) Gradually sprinkle with warm water while mixing until the dough becomes soft and pliable.
15) Divide into 4 equal portions.
16) Cover dough with a wet cloth, and set aside.
17) In a food processor, finely grind the almonds.
18) Measure 3 cups of the finely ground almonds into a mixing bowl, and stir together with 1 cup sugar, baking powder, vanilla powder, lemon zest, and 2 tablespoons orange flower water.
19) Mix in three eggs one at a time, stirring constantly; mix until you get a sticky, paste-like mixture.
20) Sprinkle cornstarch on the rolling surface to prevent sticking.
21) Roll each portion of dough very thinly, 1 to 2 millimeters (1/16 inch).
22) Cut the rolled dough into circles of about 10 centimeters (4 inches) in diameter each.
23) Lightly wipe the surface of each circle with cornstarch, and fit into a tart mold, cornstarch side down to prevent sticking.
24) Gently press the dough onto the sides and bottom of the mold, and trim extra dough from around the rim.
25) Fill three quarters of each mold with the almond filling.
26) Bake on the top shelf at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 20 to 25 minutes, or until the surface of the tart is golden and the dough is firm.
27) Remove the tarts from the molds as soon as they come out of the oven.
28) Dip each tart in the sugar syrup while still hot.
29) Stick a pine nut into the middle of each tart for decoration.
30) Place on a wire rack to drain.

1) Spread 1/4 cup of chocolate hazelnut onto each crepe.
2) Arrange 1 sliced banana down the center of each one.
3) Roll up, and place in a warm skillet over medium heat.
4) Let them warm up for about 90 seconds.
5) Transfer to plates, and serve topped with whipped cream.

1) In a large stockpot or turkey fryer, heat oil to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
2) Be sure to leave room for the turkey, or the oil will spill over.
3) Layer a large platter with food-safe paper bags.
4) Rinse turkey, and thoroughly pat dry with paper towels.
5) Rub Creole seasoning over turkey inside and out.
6) Make sure the hole at the neck is open at least 2 inches so the oil can flow freely through the bird.
7) Place the whole onion and turkey in drain basket.
8) The turkey should be placed in basket neck end first.
9) Slowly lower basket into hot oil to completely cover turkey.
10) Maintain the temperature of the oil at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and cook turkey for 3 1/2 minutes per pound, about 45 minutes.
11) Carefully remove basket from oil, and drain turkey.
12) Insert a meat thermometer into the thickest part of the thigh; the internal temperature must be 180 degrees F (80 degrees C).
13) Finish draining turkey on the prepared platter.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) In a medium mixing bowl, whip cream cheese until fluffy.
3) Add 1/2 cup sugar and vanilla extract.
4) Mix until smooth.
5) Add eggs.
6) Beat until all ingredients are thoroughly combined.
7) Pour mixture into pastry shells.
8) Bake in preheated oven for 20 minutes.

11) Mix well, then spread half of mixture over each pie.
12) Turn off oven.
13) Place pies in oven for 15 minutes.
14) Remove and chill overnight.
15) Before serving, top each pie with 1 cup of strawberries.

1) Measure butter and shortening onto a plate, put into freezer for about 20 minutes.
2) Measure cake flour, all-purpose flour, sugar, salt and baking powder into the bowl of a food processor.
3) Pulse for a few seconds to mix.
4) Take 1/2 of the cold butter and 1/2 of the cold shortening, put into processor with dry ingredients and pulse off and on for about 1 minute.
5) Scrape down twice while doing this.
6) Take remainder of the cold butter and cold shortening and cut in very briefly with the processor, leaving visible pea-sized chunks.
7) In a measuring cup, mix egg yolk and vinegar together, add ice cubes and water.
8) Let this get chilled, about 3 to 4 minutes.
9) Remove mixed flours and shortening from processor, put into a large mixing bowl.
10) Sprinkle approximately 4 to 5 tablespoons of this egg, water, vinegar mixture, a little at a time, mixing gently with a fork.
11) The key to this is, you do not want a wet dough, and you do not want to overmix.
12) Place this dough into plastic wrap or plastic bag, chill in refrigerator for a few minutes.
13) Remove from refrigerator and roll out.

1) Cook lasagna noodles according to package directions, omitting salt and fat; drain well.

5) Roll up noodles, jellyroll fashion, beginning at narrow ends.
6) Place lasagna rolls, seam sides down, in an 11- x 7- x 11/2-inch baking dish coated with cooking spray.
7) Cover and bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
8) To serve, spoon salsa evenly over rolls, and garnish with cilantro sprigs, if desired.

1) In a medium bowl, cream together butter or margarine and white sugar until light and fluffy.
2) Blend in egg and vanilla.
3) Sift together flour and salt.
4) Add to creamed mixture and mix well.
5) Stir in oats.
6) Divide dough in half.
7) Add peppermint extract and a few drops of food color to half of dough.
8) Chill for several hours.
9) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
10) Roll out each half of dough to 1/8 inch thickness on surface sprinkled lightly with confectioners' sugar.
11) Cut out half of each color with the 2 1/2 inch heart shaped cookie cutter, and half with a 1 1/2 inch cookie cutter.
12) Place them on unprepared cookie sheets.
13) Bake for 10 to 12 minutes in the preheated oven.
14) Remove from oven and place 1 one square (1/8) of a chocolate bar onto the center of each large heart.
15) Place small heart on top and press lightly to secure.
16) Transfer to rack to cool.

2) Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

1) Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
2) Spray a baking sheet with a thin layer of cooking spray.
3) Place squash halves cut side down on the baking sheet.
4) Bake squash 35 minutes in the preheated oven, or until a knife can be easily inserted.
5) Remove from oven, and cool.
6) Meanwhile, spray a non-stick saucepan with cooking spray.
7) Over medium heat, saute the onion and garlic until golden brown.
8) Stir in tomatoes, basil, bouillon cube, and black pepper.
9) Cook for about 15 minutes, or until you have a medium thick sauce.
10) Remove squash strands with a fork, reserving the shells.
11) Layer each half with a spoonful of the sauce, a layer of spaghetti squash strands, olives, and mozzarella cheese.
12) Repeat layers until shells are full, or until all of the ingredients are used.
13) Top with Parmesan cheese.
14) Bake for 20 minutes in the preheated oven, or until Parmesan cheese melts.

1) Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2) In a saucepan, combine chicken, carrots, peas, and celery.
3) Add water to cover and boil for 15 minutes.
4) Remove from heat, drain and set aside.
5) In the saucepan over medium heat, cook onions in butter until soft and translucent.
6) Stir in flour, salt, pepper, and celery seed.
7) Slowly stir in chicken broth and milk.
8) Simmer over medium-low heat until thick.
9) Remove from heat and set aside.
10) Place the chicken mixture in bottom pie crust.
11) Pour hot liquid mixture over.
12) Cover with top crust, seal edges, and cut away excess dough.
13) Make several small slits in the top to allow steam to escape.
14) Bake in the preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly.
15) Cool for 10 minutes before serving.

1) In a large bowl, cream together the margarine and sugar until smooth.
2) Stir in molasses and egg yolk.
3) Combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg; blend into the molasses mixture until smooth.
4) Cover, and chill for at least one hour.
5) Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
6) On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough out to 1/4 inch thickness.
7) Cut into desired shapes with cookie cutters.
8) Place cookies 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets.
9) Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven, until firm.
10) Remove from cookie sheets to cool on wire racks.
11) Frost or decorate when cool.

1) In a 1 pint glass jar or larger, combine the garlic, ginger, olive oil, rice vinegar, soy sauce, honey, and water.
2) Cover the jar with a tight fitting lid, and shake well.
3) Remove lid, and heat jar in the microwave for 1 minute just to dissolve the honey.
4) Let cool, and shake well before serving.
5) Store covered in the refrigerator.

1) Wash chicken breasts in water and then place in a pot with water just to cover the chicken.
2) Add some salt and pepper and garlic powder.
3) Let cool in the pot.
4) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
5) Wash and cut potatoes into bite size pieces and boil till almost fork tender.
6) Drain and set aside.
7) Wash celery and cut to bite-size pieces.
8) Cut onion to bite-size pieces.
9) In a large heavy skillet, over medium heat, saute celery and onion with 2 tablespoons oil, for 5 to 8 minutes.
10) Add the frozen vegetables and cook another 5 minutes.
11) Add flour and cook about 30 seconds.
12) Add chicken broth and bring to a boil.
13) After it has become thick, add potatoes.
14) Remove chicken from pot and cut into bite-size pieces and add to vegetable mixture.
15) Add salt and pepper to taste.
16) Pour mixture into a 9 inch deep dish pie plate and cover with pie shell.
17) Make sure you crimp the edges of the pie shell to the plate so no juices spill in oven.
18) Bake at 350  degrees F (175 degrees C) for 45 minutes or until pie shell is cooked and golden brown.

1) In a saucepan over low heat, combine the butter, sugar and 1 cup chopped almonds.
2) Stir constantly until mixture boils, then do not stir or shake.
3) Heat to 300 to 310 degrees F (149 to 154 degrees C), or until a small amount of syrup dropped into cold water forms hard, brittle threads.
4) Pour onto a large buttered cookie sheet.
5) Immediately press chocolate chips onto the hot candy. As the chocolate melts, spread it into a coating over the candy.
6) Sprinkle finely chopped almonds over the top; cool, and break into uneven pieces.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Line a pie plate with pastry.
3) Peel, core, and slice the apples.
4) Combine apples and cranberry sauce in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
5) Combine brown sugar, flour, cinnamon, and nutmeg; add to the apple mixture.
6) Mix thoroughly.
7) Turn filling into the pastry lined pan.
8) Cover with top crust.
9) Crimp edges.
10) Cut slits in top crust.
11) Bake for 1 hour, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling bubbly.

1) Heat oil in a large pot; brown chicken.
2) Remove chicken and set aside.
3) Saute onions until soft, about 5 minutes.
4) Add broth, beans, tomatoes, celery, carrots, wine, bay leaf, herbs and all the chicken; cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
5) Add parsley, cilantro, salt, and pepper, and simmer 5 more minutes.

1) Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
2) Mix in the yogurt and vinegar.
3) Place the onion in the skillet, and cook until tender.
4) Mix in the garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes.
5) Cook and stir until tomatoes are tender.
6) Season with garam masala, mint, salt, and pepper, and mix in the cilantro.
7) Place the chicken in the skillet.

9) Bring the water and rice to a boil in a large pot.
10) Mix in the bay leaf, green cardamom, black cardamom, and cinnamon.
11) Season with salt to taste.
12) Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer 20 minutes.
13) In a separate pot, alternate the rice and chicken mixture in layers, topping with rice.
14) Sprinkle with the food coloring, and mix to serve.

1) Preheat grill for high heat.

3) Stir in lime juice and zest.
4) In a small bowl, combine cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt.

1) In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook pasta until al dente, rinse under cold water and drain.
2) In a large bowl, combine the pasta, mayonnaise and mix well.
3) Stir in cucumber, onion, ham and cheese.
4) Mix well.
5) Drizzle oil and vinegar over top and toss.
6) Refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

1) Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
2) In a hot skillet, melt the butter.
3) Stir in rosemary, salt and pepper.
4) Coat potatoes evenly with the melted butter.
5) Arrange the potatoes in a single layer on a baking pan.
6) Bake in a preheated oven until potatoes are golden brown, approximately 20 to 25 minutes.
7) Toss them occasionally to ensure that they brown on all sides.

1) In a medium bowl, stir together the oats, flour, baking soda and brown sugar.

1) Heat peanut oil in a wok or large skillet.
2) When oil begins to smoke, quickly stir in 2 cloves minced garlic, ginger root, green onions and salt.
3) Stir fry until onion becomes translucent, about 2 minutes.
4) Add chicken and stir until opaque, about 3 minutes.
5) Add sweet onions, cabbage, bell pepper, peas and 1/2 cup of the broth/water and cover.
6) In a small bowl, mix the remaining 1/2 cup broth/water, soy sauce, sugar and cornstarch.
7) Add sauce mixture to wok/skillet and stir until chicken and vegetables are coated with the thickened sauce.
8) Serve immediately, over hot rice if desired.

1) Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
2) Grease one 10 inch tube pan.
3) Beat together the oil, eggs, vanilla and sugar.
4) Sift together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg.
5) Add to egg mixture; stir in apples, nuts and raisins.
6) Pour into prepared pan and bake at 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) for 1 1/2 hrs or until a cake tester inserted in the center comes out clean.
7) Cool and frost with cream cheese icing.
8) Sprinkle top with 1/4 cup fine chopped nuts.

5) Before removing from heat, stir in 1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley.
6) Add salt and pepper, to taste.

1) Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
2) Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
3) Stir in the mushrooms, green onions, garlic and cayenne pepper.
4) Cook 10 minutes, or until tender.
5) Transfer the mushroom mixture to a medium bowl.
6) Blend in the cream cheese and crabmeat.
7) On a lightly floured flat surface, roll each pastry sheet into a 12x12 inch square.
8) Cut each sheet into nine 4x4 inch squares.
9) Place 1 tablespoon of the mushroom mixture onto each pastry square.
10) Fold the squares by bringing the corners to the center, creating an X. Place the squares on a medium baking sheet.
11) Bake 20 minutes in the preheated oven, or until golden brown.

9) Refrigerate the finished apple butter in sterile containers.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) In a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish, combine mayonnaise, sour cream, soup mix, artichoke hearts, cheese and crab meat.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Melt 1/2 cup butter and heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
3) Cook and stir the mushroom slices in the skillet until tender.
4) Remove from heat, cover to keep warm, and set aside.
5) Melt the remaining butter and heat the remaining oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat.
6) Cook and stir the garlic until tender, then gradually whisk in the flour.
7) Increase heat to high, and pour in the beef broth and Marsala wine.
8) Season with kosher salt and pepper, and whisk in the browning sauce.
9) Bring to a boil, and reduce heat to low.
10) Mix in the mushrooms, reserving remaining butter and oil in the skillet.
11) Cover saucepan, remove from heat, and set aside.
12) Season chicken with salt and pepper, and dredge in the remaining flour.
13) Cook the chicken 2 minutes per side, until browned.
14) Arrange the chicken in the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish, and cover with the sauce and mushroom mixture.
15) Cover baking dish, and bake 25 minutes in the preheated oven, or until chicken juices run clear.

1) In a large skillet, cook potatoes, ham and onion in butter, stirring frequently, until potatoes are lightly browned.
2) Add broccoli; heat through.
3) Season with salt and pepper.
4) Serve with sour cream if desired.

1) In a large saucepan over medium high heat, combine the chicken meat, chicken broth, salt and pepper.
2) Bring to a boil and reduce heat to low.
3) Cover and let simmer for 30 minutes, or until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear.
4) Remove the chicken and let cool.
5) Pour the remaining chicken broth mixture into a measuring cup.
6) Let stand; spoon off fat.
7) Add enough milk to the broth mixture to equal 2 1/2 cups.
8) Cut chicken into 1/2 inch pieces.
9) In the same pan, melt butter or margarine over medium heat.
10) Add the onion and celery.
11) Saute, stirring, for 3 minutes.
12) Stir in flour until well blended.
13) Gradually stir in broth mixture.
14) Simmer, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and boils.
15) Add the chicken, vegetables, parsley and thyme.
16) Pour mixture into a 1 1/2 quart deep casserole dish.
17) Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
18) Roll out pastry 1 inch larger than the diameter of the casserole dish on a lightly floured surface.
19) Cut slits in the pastry for venting air.
20) Place pastry on top of casserole.
21) Roll edges and cut away extra pastry; flute edges by pinching together.
22) Brush pastry with beaten egg and bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
23) Let cool for 10 minutes and serve.

4) Top with remaining bread.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2) Grease a 9x13 inch pan.
3) Sift together the flour, baking soda and cinnamon.
4) Set aside.
5) In a large bowl, combine the sugar and oil until blended.
6) Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla.
7) Stir in the flour mixture just until incorporated.
8) Fold in the pineapple, carrots, coconut and walnuts.
9) Pour batter into prepared pan.
10) Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean.
11) While still warm, poke holes in the cake with a fork.
12) For the glaze: In a saucepan, combine butter, sugar, buttermilk and vanilla.
13) Bring mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce heat and cook for 5 minutes.
14) Pour glaze over warm cake, then allow to cool completely.

1) In a mixing bowl, cream butter and confectioners' sugar.
2) Add vanilla.
3) Gradually add flour; mix well.
4) With lightly floured hands, shape tablespoonfuls of batter into cookies.
5) Place cookies apart on ungreased baking sheets.
6) Bake at 350 degrees F for 9-11 minutes or until edges and bottom are lightly browned.
7) Cool for 2-3 minutes before removing to wire racks.
8) In a microwave-safe bowl, melt chocolate chips and shortening; stir until smooth.
9) Drizzle chocolate over half of the cookies.
10) Dip one end of remaining cookies into chocolate, then sprinkle with walnuts.

1) Wrap 1/2 slice of bacon around each piece of hot dog.
2) Secure the bacon with a toothpick.
3) Place hot dogs into a slow cooker on low heat.
4) Pour brown sugar over hot dogs, let cook for 5 to 6 hours; until the bacon is cooked.

1) In a large bowl, combine the chicken, broccoli, onions, bell pepper, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper and garlic.
2) Mix all together.
3) Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
4) Cover a cookie sheet with aluminum foil.
5) Place a glass upside down in the center of the cookie sheet.
6) Roll out crescent rolls around the base of the glass, with pointy ends away from the glass; when you're finished, the arrangement will look like the sun.
7) Spoon some of the chicken mixture onto the thick part of each crescent roll.
8) Fold the pointy end of each roll over the top of the mixture and tuck in the middle.
9) Remove glass from cookie sheet.
10) Arrangement of rolls will now look like a fluted tube cake.
11) Bake in preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes, or until rolls are golden brown.

1) In a large bowl, mix together the ground beef, saltine crackers and milk.
2) Season with garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper, and mix until well blended.
3) Line a 10x15 inch jellyroll pan with waxed paper.
4) Press the beef mixture firmly into the pan.
5) Cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate 8 to 10 hours, or overnight.
6) Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
7) Remove plastic wrap from meat, and rub flour over the top side of the beef.
8) Flip out of the pan onto waxed paper, and rub flour on the other side as well.
9) Cut into pieces (I use a pizza cutter).
10) Heat oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
11) Fry the meat until browned on each side, turning only once.
12) Remove to a 9x13 inch baking dish.
13) In a medium bowl, mix together the water, condensed soup, and gravy mix.
14) Pour over the meat in the dish.
15) Cover the dish loosely with aluminum foil.
16) Bake for 1 hour in the preheated oven.
17) Serve fake steak and gravy with potatoes, rice, or noodles.

1) Place the beans in a saucepan with enough water to cover them by one inch.
2) Bring beans to a slow boil.
3) Reduce heat to low, and simmer until tender but not mushy (about 35 minutes).
4) Set aside to cool.
5) When the beans have cooled, place them in a large bowl.
6) Add the celery, carrots, parsley, white onion, and mint; toss to blend.
7) For dressing, blend olive oil, orange and lemon juice, garlic, coriander, salt, pepper, and brown sugar in a blender for 6 seconds.
8) Transfer to a small saucepan, and simmer over low heat for five minutes.
9) Remove from heat, and cool.
10) Pour dressing over the bean salad, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
2) In a medium bowl, mix together 2/3 cup butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 1/4 cup flour until evenly crumbly.
3) Press into 9" square baking pan.
4) Bake for 20 minutes.
5) In a 2 quart saucepan, combine 1/2 cup butter, brown sugar, corn syrup, and sweetened condensed milk.
6) Bring to a boil.
7) Continue to boil for 5 minutes.
8) Remove from heat and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon for about 3 minutes.
9) Pour over baked crust (warm or cool).
10) Cool until it begins to firm.
11) Melt chocolate and pour over caramel layer.
12) Cover the layer completely.
13) Chill.
14) Cut into squares (about 48 - small because it is rich).

1) Preheat oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
2) Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
3) Draw a 9 inch circle on the parchment paper.
4) In a large bowl, beat egg whites until stiff but not dry.
5) Gradually add in the sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating well after each addition.
6) Beat until thick and glossy.
7) Overbeaten egg whites lose volume and deflate when folded into other ingredients.
8) Be absolutely sure not a particle of grease or egg yolk gets into the whites.
9) Gently fold in vanilla extract, lemon juice and cornstarch.
10) Spoon mixture inside the circle drawn on the parchment paper.
11) Working from the center, spread mixture toward the outside edge, building edge slightly.
12) This should leave a slight depression in the center.
13) Bake for 1 hour.
14) Cool on a wire rack.
15) Remove the paper, and place meringue on a flat serving plate.
16) Fill the center of the meringue with whipped cream, sweetened if desired.
17) Top whipped cream with kiwifruit slices.

1) In a bowl, cut margarine into flour until crumbly.

7) Carefully spread over the crust.
8) In a mixing bowl, combine milk and pudding mix.
9) Beat on low speed for 2 minutes.
10) Let stand for 2-3 minutes.
11) Spread over the cream cheese.
12) Top with the remaining whipped topping.

1) Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
2) Stir in the onion, bell pepper, carrot, and garlic, and cook 5 minutes, until tender.
3) Mix in 1 can black beans and chicken broth.
4) In a blender, puree remaining can of beans until smooth.
5) Mix into the pot.
6) Bring soup to a boil.
7) Reduce heat to low.
8) Mix in ham, cumin, salt, and pepper.
9) Simmer 20 minutes.
10) Garnish with Cheddar cheese and sour cream to serve.

1) Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
2) Drop in potatoes and cook until tender but still firm, about 15 minutes.
3) Drain, cool slightly, and peel.
4) Season with salt, then mash potatoes with fork.
5) Place in large bowl, and stir in egg and olive oil.
6) Knead in enough flour to make a soft dough.
7) On a floured surface, roll dough into a long rope.
8) Cut the rope into 1/2-inch pieces.
9) Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil.
10) Drop in gnocchi, and cook until they float to the top, about 3 to 5 minutes.
11) Serve with pasta sauce.

1) To Make Glaze: In a medium bowl combine the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, rum, mustard and garlic.
2) Season with salt and pepper to taste and mix well.
3) Place chicken pieces in a lightly oiled 9x13 inch baking dish; brush both sides with prepared glaze, using about 1/2 of the glaze.
4) Cover dish and refrigerate to marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
5) Also, refrigerate remaining glaze.
6) Preheat oven to 375  degrees F (190 degrees C).
7) Lightly brush chicken pieces on one side with some of the reserved glaze and bake uncovered in preheated oven for about 25 minutes.
8) Turn pieces, brush with remaining glaze and bake for another 25 minutes or until chicken is tender.
9) Preheat oven to broil.
10) Put chicken under broiler and lightly brown on both sides, about 2 to 3 minutes each side.
